Author: P.Sree Sudha

The Honourable Smt. Justice P.Sree Sudha
 M.A.C.M.A.No.3251 of 2008
J U D G M E N T:

This Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act,
1988 against the Judgment and Decree dated 12.03.2007 passed in M.V.O.P.No.559 of 2005 passed by the learned XVII Additional Chief Judge-cum-III Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge,
Hyderabad.

entities.text:
XVII Additional Chief Judge-cum-III Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge,
Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 02. The appellant/petitioner filed O.P.No.559 of 2005, claiming compensation of Rs.3,00,000/- for injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 22.12.2004.
The trial Court after considering the arguments of both sides, granted compensation of Rs.1,65,400/-.
Aggrieved by the said Judgment, petitioner therein preferred the present appeal.
There is no dispute regarding the accident, but the quantum of the compensation is only disputed, this Court is no going into other details.

03. The evidence of PW1, the petitioner, PW2 the Medical Officer, and the contents of Exs.A1, A2,
A5 and A7 would go to prove that in the said accident the petitioner sustained one lacerated injury on the right fore head, one lacerated injury on the right ankle and also laceration on the left leg and among them Injury No.3 is grievous in nature being fractures on left proximal tibia and fracture shaft left tibia.
During the cross-examination of PW2 Dr.Kamraj, who treated PW1, it is elicited that two fractures were in one bone on left leg, but at different places.
PW1 in the said accident received three injuries out of which Injury No.3 being the fractures of left proximal tibia and shaft left tibia are grievous in nature.

04. PW2 Dr.Kamraj, has deposed that the petitioner was admitted in their hospital on 22.12.2004 for treatment of two fractures of left leg, was operated on 27.12.2004 by way of Dynamic compression plating and buttress plating and discharged on 01.01.2005, with an advise to take medicines, physiotherapy and to come for review for follow up treatment.

The evidence of PWs1 and 2 is corroborated by the contents of Ex.A7 discharge summary of Department of Orthopaedics,
Kamineni Hospital proved through PW2.
The petitioner underwent treatment in Kamineni Hospital as inpatient for about 10 days.
Taking into consideration the nature of the injuries, the petitioner requires bed rest at least for two months.

sentences.text: 1 suffering.
Apart from that he is also entitled for an amount of Rs.15,000/- instead of Rs.6,000/- for loss of earnings during bed rest.

An amount of Rs.59,400/- can be awarded for loss of future earnings due to disability and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of amenities and he is also entitled for Rs.50,000/- towards medical expenses, Rs.10,000/- towards transportation charges and Rs.5,000/-
towards extra nourishment and an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards attendant charges.

06. Therefore, the appellant/petitioner is entitled for the compensation in the following terms:
1. Pain and Suffering Rs.30,000/-

2 . Loss of Amenities Rs.15,000/-
3. Medical Expenses Rs.50,000/-
4. Transportation Charges Rs.10,000/-
5. Extra nourishment Rs.5,000/-
6. Loss of earnings due to disability Rs.59,400/-
7. Loss of earnings during bed rest Rs.15,000/-
8.

Attendant charges Rs.10,000/-
 TOTAL Rs.1,94,400/-
 07.

In the result, the Motor Accident Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount from Rs.1,65,400/- to Rs.1,94,400/- (Rupees One Lakh Ninety Four Thousand Four Hundred only) with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing the petition till date of realization.
Respondent Nos.1 and 2/corporation shall deposit the entire amount within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a copy of this Judgment.
On such deposit, the appellant is entitled to withdraw the said amount along with interest accrued thereon.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
